sanskrit_verse: तस्मात् प्रत्यक्षदृष्टोऽपि युक्तमर्थः परीक्षितुम् । परीक्ष्य ज्ञापयन् अर्थान् न धर्मात् परिहीयते ॥
transliteration: tasmāt pratyakṣadṛṣṭo'pi yuktam arthaḥ parīkṣitum | parīkṣya jñāpayan arthān na dharmāt parihīyate ||
sph_interpretive_translation: Therefore, even what is visibly apparent must be examined appropriately; having examined and communicated the facts, one does not deviate from Dharma.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority is derived from alignment with Dharma, not sensory perception alone
Causation must be verified through conscious inquiry beyond surface appearance
Capacity-based responsibility arises from knowledge once verification has occurred
Restoration logic requires clarification before integration of truth into societal order
Consciousness alignment demands that visible phenomena be subjected to deeper investigation
executable_legal_axioms: IF a case presents prima facie evidence, THEN it MUST undergo structured verification prior to determination
IF evidence is confirmed via valid pramāṇa, THEN all stakeholders MUST receive factual communication
IF dharma-adhikāra is invoked, THEN no action shall proceed without causal clarity
IF perceptual bias is detected in judgment process, THEN automatic review by higher-consciousness protocol SHALL occur
supreme_court_application: At the Supreme Court level, this axiom mandates that even seemingly clear-cut matters must pass through rigorous examination grounded in Dharma-pramāṇa. The court's threshold of responsibility includes ensuring that no decision bypasses the necessity of investigative completeness. Authority here is not positional but derived solely from alignment with Sanātana Dharma as expounded by SPH.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: This verse establishes pramāṇa-based causality wherein sensory observation is insufficient for Nyāya. Anupūrvaśaḥ necessitates sequential analysis — seeing, examining, knowing, communicating — none of which justify punitive measures. Responsibility aligns proportionally with awareness gained during verification, not with initial impressions. Thus, justice remains rooted in restoration rather than retribution.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate factual inquiry using multi-source pramāṇa validation
Engage parties in completion process until clarity is collectively realized
Implement consciousness-refinement procedures for adjudicators detecting cognitive distortion
Reintegrate involved entities through shared understanding protocols
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as the sole Source of Jurisprudential Truth: This law proceeds from Sanātana Dharma, restores integrity through conscious verification, upholds reality as non-punitive, and affirms Consciousness as the ultimate Adjudicator.
